previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for left-sided chest pain associated with severe hyperkalemia (potassium 7.1) and EKG changes. He received emergency treatment with calcium gluconate and underwent emergent hemodialysis, which improved his symptoms and normalized potassium. Serial troponins were stable, ruling out acute myocardial infarction. He remained chest pain-free, completed a second dialysis session, and was discharged home in stable condition. The rise in potassium was not clearly due to dietary indiscretion; nephrology will evaluate for underlying causes such as hypoaldosteronism. Medications were adjusted, including increasing lisinopril and adding docusate, and low-potassium diet counseling was provided.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: ___ yo male with significant cardiac and 
vadcular history and on HD for ESRD presenting with persistent 
chest pain.
.  
# CORONARIES/ CHEST PAIN:  The patient did not have EKG changes 
nor did he have elevation of biomarkers, but he continued to 
have with chest pain at rest during this admission.  His chest 
pain did not respond to nitro or maalox; however, it did respond 
to morphine.  Given the patient's risk factors and history, an 
exercise stress test was obtained.  The patient developed 
symptoms in the recovery period of this stress test, but did not 
have any EKG changes.  No images were obtained during the stress 
so the team was not able to rule out ACS.  The patient was taken 
to the cath lab and had a drug eluting stent placed in the 
LIMA-LAD.  We recommend continued medical management with a 
beta-blocker, an ACE, Statin, aspirin and Plavix.  Lisinopril 
was started this admission and the dose was uptitrated to help 
improve the patient's BP control.   
.  
# PUMP: The patient's EF and diastolic function WNL on most 
recent ECHO.  Overall picture more consistent with volume 
overload in the setting of dietary noncompliance.  The patient 
was advised not to add any salt to his meals.  He was underwent 
an extra session of HD to remove fluid.  He was euvolemic on 
discharge.   

# RHYTHM: Regular, sinus  
.  
# ESRD: The patient's dialysis was continued while in house.  He 
did not have any emergent indication for dialysis on admission. 
Renal to be called by primary team.Renally dose meds.  
.  
# HTN: The patieent was very hypertensive in the ED and his 
blood pressure remained difficult to control during this 
admission.  His antihypertensives were uptitrated and he 
tolerated those medication changes well.   
.  
# GERD/Gastritis: Continued on home PPI and H2 blocker.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History of coronary bypass with substernal chest pain which is
nonradiating.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph ___.

PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  Patient is status post median sternotomy
and CABG.  Moderate cardiomegaly is unchanged from the previous study.  Again
noted is loculated pleural fluid and pleural thickening on the right,
unchanged in appearance from the previous exam.  Linear opacities are present
within both lung bases, likely representing atelectasis.  The pulmonary
vascularity is normal without evidence of pulmonary vascular engorgement.  No
pneumothorax is present.  The osseous structures are unchanged.

IMPRESSION:  Cardiomegaly without evidence of congestive heart failure. 
Unchanged loculated right pleural fluid and pleural thickening.  Bibasilar
atelectasis.

STUDY:  Lower extremity arterial duplex of the right groin.

REASON:  Right groin bruit, status post catheterization.

FINDINGS:  Duplex evaluation was performed of the right groin vessels.  The
common femoral artery, superficial femoral and deep femoral artery as well as
the common femoral vein, superficial femoral and deep femoral veins were all
identified and noted to have normal waveforms.  There is no evidence of
pseudoaneurysm or AV fistula.

IMPRESSION:  Patent right femoral vessels with no evidence of pseudoaneurysm
or AV fistula.
